name: AL-06
label: Safe R

Incumbent Gary Palmer holds a massive fundraising edge over a challenger who has raised under $7,000
Prediction markets price Palmer at roughly 96 percent to win

model.rationale: The district's seventeen-point Republican lean, Palmer's million-dollar war chest against a challenger with about $6,500 raised, and market pricing near 96 percent Republican all point the same direction. With no polls or ratings suggesting anything different, this stays firmly Safe Republican.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal, a late infusion of outside spending against Palmer, or a dramatic national environment shift would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District, covering the Birmingham suburbs, leans about seventeen points Republican, placing it among the most strongly Republican House seats in the country. Incumbent Gary Palmer is seeking re-election and has raised more than one million dollars with no outside groups opposing him. His Democratic challenger, Maurice Mercer, has reported roughly six thousand five hundred dollars raised and under two thousand on hand, leaving him badly outmatched financially.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Palmer about a 96 percent chance of winning. The district's heavy Republican lean, the incumbent's financial advantage, and the challenger's minimal campaign leave Mercer without an evident path. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with the main open question being the size of Palmer's eventual winning margin.
